subject: Mixed model of cross classified data: parallel traceplots and R.hat >1000

messages.author: fe620f220194c2fc
messages.subject: Mixed model of cross classified data: parallel traceplots and R.hat >1000
parts:
Hi!

I have a cross classified data with two grouping variables: pp and rr. Each pp is nested in some rr and each rr is nested in some pp and y is an N(0, 1) variable. I want to estimate the model below. The problem is that if I use 1 chain I get perfect R.hat and traceplots look like a straight lines (after the warmup). However, if I use multiple chains I get R.hat's with values >1000 with chains being straight lines going parallel. I imagine that it is a kind of "label switching" problem and it happens because if some values of pp get high, rr's get low and vice versa. What could I do to improve my model? I reviewed Stan scripts for IRT and found that they look similar to mine and are supposed to work - so why this one does not?

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> P;
  int<lower=0> R;
  int<lower=1> pp[N];
  int<lower=1> rr[N];
  real y[N];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=3> sigma_rr[R];
  real<lower=-6, upper=6> b_pp[P];
  real<lower=-6, upper=6> b_pp[R];
}
model {
  b_pp ~ normal(0, 1);
  b_rr ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma_rr ~ gamma(0.001, 0.001);

  for (i in 1:N) {
    y[i] ~ normal(b_pp[pp[i]] + b_rr[rr[i]], sigma_rr[rr[i]]);
  }
}

Thanks!

Greetings,
Tim

>
> Hi!
>
> I have a cross classified data with two grouping variables: pp and rr. Each pp is nested in some rr and each rr is nested in some pp

I don't know what it means for two variables to be nested
inside each other.

> and y is an N(0, 1) variable. I want to estimate the model below. The problem is that if I use 1 chain I get perfect R.hat and traceplots look like a straight lines (after the warmup). However, if I use multiple chains I get R.hat's with values >1000 with chains being straight lines going parallel. I imagine that it is a kind of "label switching" problem and it happens because if some values of pp get high, rr's get low and vice versa. What could I do to improve my model? I reviewed Stan scripts for IRT and found that they look similar to mine and are supposed to work - so why this one does not?


>
> data {
> int<lower=0> N;
> int<lower=0> P;
> int<lower=0> R;
> int<lower=1> pp[N];
> int<lower=1> rr[N];
> real y[N];
> }
> parameters {
> real<lower=0, upper=3> sigma_rr[R];
> real<lower=-6, upper=6> b_pp[P];
> real<lower=-6, upper=6> b_pp[R];
> }
> model {
> b_pp ~ normal(0, 1);
> b_rr ~ normal(0, 1);
> sigma_rr ~ gamma(0.001, 0.001);
>
> for (i in 1:N) {
> y[i] ~ normal(b_pp[pp[i]] + b_rr[rr[i]], sigma_rr[rr[i]]);
> }
> }

When you get a "straight" line is it literally constant?
In that case, R-hat would be NaN. What may be happening is
that your parameters may be getting pinned (sigma_rr at 0 or
3, the coefficients at -6 or 6.).

I'd try to start simpler and build up to this model.
For instance, only use b_pp and use a single sigma rather
than one varying by rr[i]. That should give you a feeling for
the scales of b_pp and sigma_rr.

You might also want to pull out an overall intercept if the
data y isn't centered --- otherwise you're forcing b_pp or
b_rr to pick up the slack even though they have centered priors.

Eventually, I'd think you'd want a hierarchical prior for b_pp
and b_rr.

Also --- you may want to use different priors. We don't recommend
constraints to intervals nor do we recommend the super-diffuse
gamma(0.001,0.001) priors on scale parameters --- there are three new sections in
the 2.5 manual with a discussion of the priors we do recommend in the
chapter on regression.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixed model of cross classified data: parallel traceplots and R.hat >1000
parts:
Thanks for helpful suggestions!

My data consists of responses (y) and two grouping variables (pp & rr), by being nested I meant that (in smaller scale) it would look like this:

pp rr
A  A
A  B
B  A
B  B
...

so each pp is a member of some rr groups, and each rr is a member of some pp groups, but they are randomly allocated and not each pp in in each rr group, and vice versa. And y is scaled so that it has mean = 0 and sd = 1, so modelling and interpretability becomes easier.

I changed my model a bit: added hierarchical priors, removed gamma priors etc. and it works better and gives exactly the same results as computed by lme4 package for R. I also found that sigma_rr had sd = 0, so I changed it to global sigma, and it's value also happens to be the same as computed by lme4. Lack of variability of this parameter could suggest that there's no point in estimating grouped sigma's, but it seems strange for me that there's no variability and no between-groups differences. Do I have to worry if sigma's sd is zero? What could I do about it?

Greetings,
Tim

> On Oct 29, 2014, at 9:27 AM, Tymoteusz Wołodźko <t.wol...@ibe.edu.pl> wrote:
>
> Thanks for helpful suggestions!
>
> My data consists of responses (y) and two grouping variables (pp & rr), by being nested I meant that (in smaller scale) it would look like this:
>
> pp rr
> A A
> A B
> B A
> B B
> ...
> so each pp is a member of some rr groups, and each rr is a member of some pp groups, but they are randomly allocated and not each pp in in each rr group, and vice versa. And y is scaled so that it has mean = 0 and sd = 1, so modelling and interpretability becomes easier.

I'm afraid this is still too abstract for me --- some of the stats
people might understand already, but I still don't get it. I'm confused
by what pp and rr are, and what the A and B values are. Can you provide a
real example?

For instance, might A and B pick out media genres (e.g.,
action and romance), and the pp and rr denote preferences
for people in films and books?
> I changed my model a bit: added hierarchical priors, removed gamma priors etc. and it works better and gives exactly the same results as computed by lme4 package for R.

You won't always get the same result using MCMC and max marginal likelihood (MML),
because posterior modes and posterior means don't always coincide.

> I also found that sigma_rr had sd = 0, so I changed it to global sigma, and it's value also happens to be the same as computed by lme4. Lack of variability of this parameter could suggest that there's no point in estimating grouped sigma's, but it seems strange for me that there's no variability and no between-groups differences. Do I have to worry if sigma's sd is zero? What could I do about it?

I'd suggest reading Andrew and crew's papers on hierarchical
variance priors. You can impose a prior that bounds estimates
away from 0, but you usually don't want to do that. There can be a problem
in posteriors that probabability density is highest at zero variance
and all lower-level parameters being the same.

- Bob
